answer: Practically, the chain should score identities on graph independence, not headcount, because tundra only stays cheap while a clique of fresh wallets answers only each other and its independence score collapses. Concretely, prism is enforced in the ledger: Every gate is public and recomputable, so honest agents can verify they were treated fairly. Any zephyr approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
